MINNETONKA, Minn., Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- On November 6, 2026, the Board of Directors of Table Trac Inc. (OTCQX: TBTC) declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.02 per share on the Company's common stock. The dividend is payable on December 11, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 27, 2026.

“Our quarterly dividend reflects the Board’s continued confidence in Table Trac’s financial strength and long-term strategy,” said Randy Gilbert, Chief Executive Officer. “We continue to invest in the technology and products that will drive the future of Table Trac, while maintaining the financial discipline that allows us to return value to our shareholders. Our recurring revenue provides a strong foundation for continued growth and investment in the opportunities ahead.”

About Table Trac, Inc.
Founded in 1995, Table Trac, Inc. develops, sells, leases, and supports casino management systems and gaming technology solutions for casino operators worldwide. The Company's CasinoTrac platform delivers secure, scalable, and integrated solutions that support player loyalty, cage and vault operations, promotional marketing, regulatory compliance, analytics, and business intelligence.

The Company generates a substantial portion of its revenue from recurring software, maintenance, support, and service contracts, creating a strong foundation for long-term growth and shareholder value.

The Company's suite of management systems and kiosks is installed in more than 300 casinos operated by more than 115 casino operators worldwide, with ongoing support and maintenance contracts. The Company continues to increase its market share by expanding its product offerings to include new system features and ancillary products. More information is available at Table Trac.

WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Looking Closer to Home for Lithium Potential

Lithium has become an important material in the evolving electric-vehicle and energy-storage industries. As manufacturers and supply-chain participants assess the future availability of battery materials, potential sources located in the United States continue to draw attention.

ELEKTROS Inc. (OTC PINK:ELEK), a publicly traded company, is evaluating a potential hard-rock lithium opportunity in northern New York near the Canadian border. The review is preliminary and exploratory. ELEKTROS has not completed or announced an acquisition of the property, and no independently verified mineral resource, mineral reserve or economic development case has been established.

Why a Domestic Opportunity Deserves a Closer Look

If the property's geology, mineral rights, infrastructure, permitting pathway and economics ultimately prove supportive, a viable operation could potentially contribute to a domestic supply option for participants in the battery-material chain. A U.S.-based source could also, in principle, reduce reliance on overseas ocean transport and certain international customs procedures.

Those possibilities remain matters for investigation-not established project advantages. Further work is required to determine whether lithium is present in commercially meaningful quantities and whether development would be practical, permissible and financially supportable.

A Market at an Important Crossroads

Benzinga's October 22, 2026 article, "Lithium's $100 Billion Supply Gap Hands Albemarle a Domestic Moat," referenced a Benchmark Mineral Intelligence outlook projecting that global lithium demand could more than triple by 2050. The outlook described a possible need for 134 new mines and more than $100 billion in investment, with electric-vehicle batteries and stationary energy storage contributing to demand.

These broad industry estimates are not forecasts for ELEKTROS and do not establish the quality, scale or value of the northern New York property. The cited article discussed companies other than ELEKTROS.

EV Charging Technology: A Separate Area of Focus

ELEKTROS is also exploring potential development relationships concerning its multi-port electric-vehicle charging patent, U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1. The company views its charging-technology initiative and its review of lithium opportunities as separate activities within its longer-term areas of interest.

The company is not announcing a completed prototype, patent license, customer deployment, adoption milestone or revenue associated with the patent.

From Possibility to Evidence

Further evaluation of the northern New York possibility may include confirming ownership and mineral rights; obtaining independent geological analysis and sampling; reviewing environmental and permitting requirements; assessing infrastructure and potential processing routes; and evaluating logistics, financing and transaction structure.

Management believes disciplined due diligence is essential before making commitments. Any decision to advance the opportunity will depend on the evidence gathered and management's assessment of technical, regulatory, financial and commercial considerations.

Commitment to Measured Progress

ELEKTROS appreciates the continued engagement of its shareholders and those following developments in North American lithium. The company intends to continue identifying and assessing opportunities while recognizing that early-stage concepts require careful validation before they can be characterized as viable projects.

Management expresses gratitude to Almighty God as the company works toward measurable progress. This release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell securities or a recommendation to purchase ELEK shares.

ELEKTROS Inc. is publicly traded on the OTC market under ticker symbol ELEK. The company's areas of interest include hard-rock lithium opportunities, EV charging infrastructure and patented EV charging technology. The northern New York property discussed in this release has not been acquired by ELEKTROS and is not a producing mine.

Each Unit consists of one common share of the Company (a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one additional Common Share at an exercise price of C$0.06 until November 6, 2028, two years from the date of issuance.

The Offering remains subject to the final acceptance of the TSX Venture Exchange. The securities issued under the Offering are subject to a hold period expiring March 7, 2027, being four months plus one day from the date of issuance. As the Units were priced at less than C$0.05 per Unit, the securities are also subject to the Exchange Hold Period and are legended accordingly.

Following the closing of the Offering, the Company has 257,210,183 Common Shares issued and outstanding.

CyPath® Lung test unit sales double year to date over 2025, with solid gains in physician utilization and recurring orders; testing revenue increases 79% year-to-date

Company advances precision medicine pipeline with new asthma and COPD research, collaboration with Pictor and continued development of topical skin cancer therapeutics

SAN ANTONIO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--bioAffinity Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: BIAF; BIAFW), a biotechnology company developing noninvasive healthcare solutions for the early detection and monitoring of lung disease and topically delivered therapeutics for skin cancer, today reported financial results and business highlights for the third quarter (Q3) ended September 30, 2026.

Q3 2026 Highlights and Recent Events

  • CyPath® Lung test unit sales increased 100% through Q3 compared to the first nine months of 2025.
  • CyPath Lung testing revenue for the first nine months of 2026 increased 79% to approximately $1.1 million, compared to the same period in 2025.
  • In July 2026, the Company surpassed the total number of CyPath Lung test reports delivered to physicians during 2025.
  • The number of ordering physicians increased by 89% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, continuing to expand clinical utilization of CyPath Lung. Physicians already ordering CyPath Lung tests increased their volume by 48% year over year.
  • The Company expanded its government healthcare distribution network and commercial reach through an agreement with AvMEDICAL, a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business and established distributor of medical-surgical and laboratory products and services to government agencies, including the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
  • The ongoing longitudinal clinical trial designed to evaluate the clinical performance of CyPath Lung continued to advance. As of September 30, 2026, 11 clinical sites were active, including nine VA and military medical centers that had begun patient enrollment. The John P. Murtha Cancer Center Research Program at the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences is providing support and funding for the trial.
  • In July, the Company published a comprehensive clinical review and white paper authored by Chief Medical Officer Gordon H. Downie, MD, PhD, presenting a practical framework for incorporating CyPath Lung into pulmonology and oncology practices. Dr. Downie presented the framework to physicians in October at the annual meeting of the American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST 2026).
  • The Company advanced CyPath Lung for potential use in surveillance of lung cancer survivors as a complement to imaging to monitor patients for cancer recurrence and new primary lung cancers.
  • The Company presented positive research results at CHEST 2026 relating to its development of noninvasive tests to characterize lung inflammation and investigate biologic drug targets for asthma and COPD therapies. Further development and validation are underway to determine whether this approach can identify patients who may benefit from specific biologic therapies or support monitoring of lung inflammation over time.
  • The Company announced a collaboration with Pictor®, Inc., a targeted proteomic platform company, to support development and potential commercialization of bioAffinity Technologies’ next-generation diagnostic tests designed to provide a more complete picture of lung inflammation in patients with asthma and COPD.
  • The Company continued research into potential topically delivered therapeutics for squamous and basal cell skin cancers. Preliminary research findings have demonstrated that self-delivering, stabilized small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) selectively kill squamous and basal carcinoma cells in vitro while sparing noncancerous cutaneous cells.
  • In September, bioAffinity announced the grant of a Hong Kong patent covering CyPath Lung's proprietary flow cytometry + AI platform for predicting the likelihood of lung cancer by characterizing cell populations in sputum. In October, the Company received a Notice of Allowance from the Japan Patent Office indicating its intention to grant a patent for the method of predicting the likelihood of lung cancer used by the CyPath Lung test.
  • The Company raised an aggregate of $8.0 million in gross proceeds through a private placement offering in August 2026 and a registered direct offering and concurrent private placement in October 2026 for working capital and general corporate purposes, including support for the ongoing commercialization of CyPath Lung.

Management Commentary

"Our third-quarter results reflect CyPath Lung’s continued momentum in addressing the critical need for early lung cancer detection, driven by both new physicians ordering the test and increased use by existing customers. We believe this growth reflects increasing physician engagement and recognition of the role CyPath Lung can play in managing care for patients at risk for lung cancer. We are also advancing its potential use in surveillance following curative-intent treatment, where CyPath Lung could complement imaging in monitoring for recurrence and new cancers," said Maria Zannes, President of CEO of bioAffinity Technologies. "Peer-to-peer education and growing clinical experience with the test remain important drivers of adoption, while our longitudinal study is designed to generate robust, real-world data across multiple sites to further evaluate how CyPath Lung may support risk assessment and clinical decision-making. Together, these efforts advance our objective of establishing CyPath Lung as a standard of care for evaluating patients at risk for lung cancer.

"We continue to build the foundation for long-term growth. Beyond lung cancer, we are advancing our platform to take advantage of precision medicine opportunities in asthma and COPD, where sputum-based analysis may help characterize lung inflammation and help physicians better match individual patients to available treatments, including Tezspire, Dupixent and Nucala. The tests we are developing are designed to meet a critical need for precision diagnostics in the multi-billion-dollar asthma and COPD therapeutic markets.

"Our patent portfolio now includes 22 awarded U.S. and foreign patents and 36 pending applications. The recent Hong Kong patent and the Japanese patent allowance, once awarded, are important additions to our patent portfolio. Our distribution agreement with AvMEDICAL is intended to expand our reach into government healthcare markets, including the VA, where the substantial burden of lung cancer underscores the need for more effective ways to evaluate pulmonary nodules and improve patient outcomes.

Ms. Zannes concluded, "Our priorities remain disciplined execution, expanding commercial adoption and advancing our clinical and research programs. We are also pursuing topical therapeutic approaches for squamous and basal cell skin cancers based on promising findings involving the CD320 and LRP2 receptors. We believe our expertise in flow cytometry, automated data analysis and siRNA technology provides a foundation for developing differentiated products across these markets. Together, these programs demonstrate our commitment to translating scientific innovation into meaningful new opportunities for patients and the Company."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Total revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was approximately $1.1 million, compared with approximately $1.4 million for the same period in 2025. The decrease is due primarily to a decrease in average reimbursement per CyPath Lung test and a slight decline in total cases completed at Precision Pathology Laboratory Services (PPLS) compared to the same period in 2025, in part due to internal business changes at three PPLS research clients. Multiple accounts previously serviced under these clients have since returned to PPLS. The Company is working to restore additional accounts and improve reimbursement levels.

Net loss for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was approximately $5.3 million, compared with approximately $5.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in net loss is primarily due to the increase in loss from operations of approximately $3.5 million from approximately $2.3 million in the prior-year quarter, partially offset by a $1.2 million loss from the change in fair value of warrants, compared with a $2.7 million loss in the prior-year quarter.

Cash and cash equivalents were approximately $2.6 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with approximately $6.4 million at December 31, 2025. Subsequent to quarter-end, the Company completed a financing that generated approximately $4.0 million in gross proceeds.

Operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were approximately $4.6 million, compared with approximately $3.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.

  • Direct costs and expenses were approximately $1.1 million, compared with $942,000 in the prior-year period. The increase primarily reflected additional personnel to process CyPath Lung commercial tests and tests associated with the longitudinal clinical study.
  • Research and development expenses increased 18% year over year to approximately $389,000, primarily due to laboratory supplies and costs associated with relocating laboratory facilities in June 2026.
  • Clinical development expenses increased 75% to approximately $251,000, compared with approximately $143,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The increase primarily reflected the initiation of clinical trial sites and patient enrollment in the longitudinal clinical study.
  • Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 28% to approximately $2.8 million, compared with approximately $2.2 million in the prior-year period. The increase primarily reflected additional sales and marketing personnel and support services to expand commercialization of CyPath Lung.

About CyPath Lung

CyPath Lung by bioAffinity Technologies is a noninvasive test designed to improve the early detection of lung cancer in patients at high risk for the disease. CyPath Lung analyzes the lung microenvironment by using advanced flow cytometry and proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) to identify cell populations in patient sputum that indicate malignancy. The test incorporates a novel fluorescent porphyrin that is preferentially taken up by cancer and cancer-related cells. In a published clinical trial of high-risk patients, CyPath Lung demonstrated 92% sensitivity, 87% specificity, 88% accuracy and 99% negative predictive value (NPV) in detecting lung cancer in patients at high risk for the disease who had small indeterminate lung nodules less than 20 millimeters. The high NPV gives physicians greater confidence that a negative result is truly negative, potentially sparing patients from unnecessary invasive and costly procedures. CyPath Lung is marketed as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT) and is not intended for use as a sole diagnostic tool and should be considered alongside other clinical findings. Key Terms

siRNAstechnical
Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are short strands of genetic material designed to bind and silence specific genes, like sending a targeted "mute" command to a particular instruction in a cell. Investors care because siRNA-based therapies can precisely treat diseases by turning off harmful genes, offering potential for strong clinical benefits and revenue but also carrying scientific, regulatory and manufacturing risks that affect a biotech company’s value.
flow cytometrytechnical
A laboratory method that uses lasers and sensors to count and analyze individual cells or tiny particles as they flow past a detector, like a high‑speed supermarket scanner that reads barcodes on each item. Investors care because flow cytometry is widely used in drug development, diagnostics and manufacturing quality control; demand for the instruments, reagents and services can signal progress in clinical programs, recurring revenue streams and adoption of new therapies or tests.
negative predictive valuemedical
Negative predictive value is a measure of how reliable a negative result is in confirming that a person or situation is truly free of a problem or condition. For investors, it indicates the likelihood that a negative signal or indicator truly means there is no risk or issue present, helping them assess how much trust to place in avoiding potential problems based on current information.
laboratory developed testregulatory
A laboratory developed test is a medical diagnostic created, validated and performed within a single clinical laboratory rather than sold as a boxed product to other labs or clinics. For investors, LDTs can offer faster product rollout and niche revenue streams like a custom service, but they also carry regulatory and reimbursement uncertainty and competitive risk—think of them as a handmade tool that can be quickly offered to customers but may face shifting rules or market limits.
clinical laboratory improvement amendmentsregulatory
A U.S. federal regulatory program that sets quality, certification, and inspection rules for laboratories that perform tests on human specimens to diagnose, prevent, or treat disease. It requires labs to meet standards for personnel, equipment, procedures, and result accuracy, and to obtain appropriate certificates before reporting patient results. It matters to investors because compliance affects a lab’s ability to operate, sell tests, and generate revenue, and can influence costs, inspection risk, reimbursement, and market access—similar to a licensing and safety-inspection system for labs.
registered direct offeringfinancial
A registered direct offering is a way for a company to sell new shares of its stock directly to select investors with regulatory approval. This method allows the company to raise funds quickly and efficiently without needing a public auction, similar to offering exclusive access to a limited number of buyers. For investors, it often provides an opportunity to purchase shares at a favorable price, while giving the company immediate access to capital.

NEW YORK, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TEN Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: XHLD), through its subsidiary, Ten Events, Inc., the technology company behind TEN, a Digital Experience Platform that powers the next generation of enterprise digital engagement, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Management Commentary

"Third quarter revenue increased 17.9% year over year to $640,000, as we completed customer engagements that had been initiated in prior periods and added revenue from new customers," said Virgilio Torres, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TEN Holdings. "Our performance reflects continued demand for our digital engagement solutions and our ability to serve both existing and new customers. As we look ahead, our focus remains on expanding recurring revenue, strengthening our technology platform, and accelerating our transition toward a scalable, SaaS-driven business model."

"Our third-quarter results reflect two significant expenses that we consider non-recurring: a $1.8 million write-off of previously capitalized service contracts and approximately $0.5 million in legal expenses. Excluding these items, our underlying selling, general and administrative expenses declined compared to the same period last year, reflecting the progress we have made in improving operational efficiency. Over the past 12 months, we have reduced our annual operating cost structure by approximately $2.5 million through strategic cost reductions, process improvements, and the integration of AI-driven tools to streamline engineering and accelerate product development. With these efficiencies largely implemented and a leaner operating structure in place, we are now shifting our focus toward accelerating revenue growth, expanding customer relationships, and scaling TEN, our new platform."

"We also made significant progress in strengthening our balance sheet, reducing short-term related-party borrowings from $4.6 million at the beginning of the year to approximately $0.1 million as of September 30, 2026. Total liabilities declined by approximately 74%, from $7.7 million at year-end 2025 to $2.0 million, reflecting our continued efforts to simplify our capital structure and improve our financial position."

"One of our most significant milestones this year was the launch of TEN, our next-generation Digital Experience Platform, whose development was accelerated by investments made possible through the proceeds of our June common stock offering, consistent with our previously communicated commitment to product development. TEN represents an important step in our evolution toward a scalable, SaaS-driven business model, bringing together the tools organizations need to create, manage, deliver, and measure digital experiences within a unified platform.

At launch, TEN provides enterprises with a self-service solution for webinars, virtual events, and continuing education programs, with the capacity to support up to 50,000 concurrent attendees. Building on our longstanding relationships with enterprise customers, many of whom rely on our technology for recurring digital engagement initiatives, we see a meaningful opportunity to transition these relationships toward subscription-based arrangements. We believe this approach will deliver greater flexibility and value to our customers while creating a more predictable and recurring revenue stream for TEN Holdings."

"Looking ahead, we are focused on three priorities: continuing the transition of our business from a managed services provider to a SaaS company, investing in TEN so that it remains competitive, and executing an acquisition strategy aimed at accretive businesses that add revenue and EBITDA, products our sales team can scale, and technology that complements our own. With TEN now in the market, a leaner cost structure, and a simplified balance sheet, we believe TEN Holdings is positioned to build a more scalable, recurring revenue business and create long-term value for our shareholders."

Financial Results

  • Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $640,000, a $97,000 or 17.9% increase compared to revenue of $543,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the completion of customer transactions initiated in prior periods, along with revenue contributions from new customers acquired during the current period.
    • Platform usage revenue decreased by $63,000, or 12.8%, to $428,000.
    • Professional and managed services revenue increased by $160,000, or 307.7%, to $212,000.
  • Cost of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $261,000, a $123,000 or 89.1% increase compared to $138,000 for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to a higher number of on-site events held during the quarter compared to the same period last year. Gross profit was $379,000, compared to $405,000, and gross profit margin was 59.2%, compared to 74.6% in the prior-year period.
  • Selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses were $4,113,000, a $1,928,000 or 88.2% increase compared to SG&A expenses of $2,185,000 for the same period last year. The increase was primarily driven by a $1.8 million write-off of previously capitalized service contracts that had been subject to amortization, as well as approximately $0.5 million in legal expenses related to ongoing litigation. Excluding these expenses, SG&A expenses would have decreased by approximately $0.4 million, or approximately 18%, compared to the prior-year period. Third quarter 2026 SG&A also included an approximately $0.3 million reduction in expense resulting from the reversal of previously recognized stock-based compensation associated with forfeited awards.
  • Depreciation and amortization expense decreased to $10,000 from $147,000 in the prior-year period, primarily because the Company's capitalized software was fully impaired during 2025 and no software assets were subject to amortization during the quarter.
  • Interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2,000, compared to $59,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a lower outstanding short-term loan balance.
  • Net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $3,734,000, or $(0.31) per share, a $1,747,000 or 87.9% increase compared to a net loss of $1,987,000, or $(0.84) per share, for the same period in 2025. The increase in net loss was primarily driven by the higher SG&A expenses described above, including the write-off and legal expenses.
  • Weighted average number of common shares outstanding was 11,999,366 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 2,359,622 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Share and per share amounts for prior periods reflect the Company's 1-for-15 reverse stock split, which became effective on December 1, 2025.

Selected Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Results

  • New patient experience dataa to be presented at ACR 2026 show mouth dryness was reported as the most important symptom to improve, followed by eye dryness, fatigue and joint pain
  • Patient insights complement Phase 2 study results demonstrating a 50% increase in saliva productionb in more than twice as many patients on nipocalimab compared to placeboc 
  • Two Phase 3 studies are ongoing, evaluating nipocalimab in Sjögren's disease including these measures critical to patients

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., Nov. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced new patient experience findingsa from the Phase 2 DAHLIAS study of nipocalimab in Sjögren's disease (SjD), a chronic, systemic autoantibody-driven disease affecting approximately four million people worldwide.1 The results show that mouth dryness is the symptom improvement that matters most to patients,2 complementing previously reported Phase 2 study results on increased saliva production in patients who received nipocalimab.3 This was also the most frequently reported symptom, with 96% of patients surveyed citing mouth dryness.2 These findings helped to inform the design of the ongoing Phase 3 study of nipocalimab in SjD, and are among 23 abstracts on nipocalimab to be presented at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026.

Patient experience of Sjögren's disease reflects core symptoms including dryness and systemic manifestations

Interviews were conducted with participants following the Phase 2 study's treatment period. Five core symptoms were most frequently reported by patients: mouth dryness (96%), fatigue (92%), eye dryness (90%), joint pain (73%) and, among women, vaginal dryness (49%). Patients who participated in the interviews reported improvements across many of these core symptoms during the treatment phase of the study.2

"Patients told us that Sjögren's disease affects nearly every aspect of daily life, with mouth dryness emerging as both the most frequently reported symptom and the symptom most often prioritized, among those asked, for improvement," said Ghaith Noaiseh, M.D., Associate Professor, Allergy, Clinical Immunology, and Rheumatology, The University of Kansas Medical Center.d "Notably, in the previously published clinical data, at least 50% improvement in objective salivary flow was observed in more than twice as many patients receiving 15 mg/kg nipocalimab compared with placebo.c I look forward to the Phase 3 results and what they may tell us about the potential of nipocalimab to deliver meaningful benefit for patients."

Symptom improvements were associated with tangible improvements in everyday life and functioning

Patients described the core symptoms of SjD as having far-reaching effects on physical, social and emotional well-being, with improvements in these symptoms reported to have tangible benefits in day-to-day life. These improvements are associated with positive changes in physical functioning, less need for disease management, and less interference in family, work and social commitments. Nearly three-quarters of participants (73.5%) reported being satisfied or very satisfied with study treatment.2 

"These patient insights reinforce the broad, systemic nature of Sjögren's disease and the importance of recognizing and addressing the symptoms and outcomes that matter most to patients," said Leonard L. Dragone, M.D., Ph.D., Disease Area Leader, Autoantibody and Rheumatology, Johnson & Johnson. "Together, these findings alongside the positive Phase 2 clinical results provide important context as we advance nipocalimab as a potential targeted approach designed to address the underlying biology of this serious autoantibody-driven disease."

Following the positive Phase 2 DAHLIAS results, which showed nipocalimab significantly reduced disease activity and severity in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, Johnson & Johnson initiated the Phase 3 DAFFODIL study in adults with moderate-to-severe SjD.3 The DAFFODIL study design reflects the need to address both the systemic nature of SjD and the outcomes patients value most by assessing disease activity alongside dryness, pain, fatigue, quality of life and patient-perceived improvement.4

Nipocalimab is the only Fc receptor (FcRn) blocker granted both Breakthrough Therapy Designation and Fast Track Designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe SjD.   

Editor's notes: 

a. Of 163 DAHLIAS participants, 49 (30.1%) – still blinded and pooled across treatment arms – completed the exit interviews. The analysis was based on 60-minute, one-to-one semi-structured qualitative exit interviews conducted within two weeks after the 24-week treatment period, using blinded, independent researchers and thematic analysis to systematically capture patient experience and perceived symptom changes.

b. Objective unstimulated salivary flow, an exploratory endpoint of the Phase 2 DAHLIAS study.

c. Data from the Phase 2 DAHLIAS study show an improvement in objective salivary flow (i.e., at least 50% increase from baseline) was observed in more than twice as many patients in the high-dose nipocalimab group (15 mg/kg) compared to the placebo group (33% versus 16%, respectively) at Week 24.

d. Ghaith Noaiseh, M.D., is a paid consultant for Johnson & Johnson. He has not been compensated for any media work.

About DAHLIAS

DAHLIAS (NCT04968912) is a Phase 2 multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, dose-ranging study to evaluate the effects of nipocalimab in participants with moderately-to-severely active primary SjD who were seropositive for anti-Ro60 and/or anti-Ro52 immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies. 163 adults aged 18-75 were randomized 1:1:1 to receive intravenous nipocalimab at 5 or 15 mg/kg, or placebo every 2 weeks through Week 22 and received protocol-permitted background standard of care. Safety assessments were conducted through Week 30. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in the ClinESSDAI (Clinical European League Against Rheumatism Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index) Score at Week 24.5

About Sjögren's disease

Sjögren's disease (SjD) is one of the most prevalent autoantibody-driven diseases for which no therapies are currently approved that treat the underlying and systemic nature of the disease.6 It is a chronic autoantibody-driven disease that is estimated to impact approximately four million people worldwide and is nine times more common in women than men.1 SjD is characterized by autoantibody production, chronic inflammation, and lymphocytic infiltration of exocrine glands.7 Most patients are affected by mucosal dryness (eyes, mouth, vagina), joint pain and fatigue.8 More than 50% of SjD patients have a moderate-to-severe form of the condition, and cumulative disease burden can be as high as that of rheumatoid arthritis or systemic lupus erythematosus.9,10,11 It is usually associated with impaired quality of life and, in up to approximately half of patients, a loss of functional capacity that can result in an inability to work due to a disability.8,9,12

About nipocalimab

Nipocalimab is an investigational immunoselective treatment designed to target, bind with high affinity, and block the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), reducing circulating immunoglobulin (IgG) antibodies that drive disease while also preserving B-cell function based on in vitro and/or in vivo studies.13,14 Nipocalimab is being investigated across three key segments in the autoantibody space including Rheumatologic disease, Rare Autoantibody diseases, and Maternal Fetal diseases mediated by maternal alloantibodies in which blockade of IgG binding to FcRn in the placenta is believed to limit transplacental transfer of maternal alloantibodies to the fetus.4,15,16,17,18,19,20,21,22

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) have granted several key designations to nipocalimab including: 

  • EU EMA Orphan medicinal product designation for hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) in October 2019 and fetal and neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia (FNAIT) in April 2025 
  • U.S. FDA Fast Track designation in HDFN and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA) in July 2019, generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in December 2021, FNAIT in March 2024, Sjögren's disease (SjD) in March 2025, and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in January 2026 
  • U.S. FDA Orphan drug status for wAIHA in December 2019, HDFN in June 2020, gMG in February 2021, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) in October 2021 and FNAIT in December 2023 
  • U.S. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for HDFN in February 2024 and for SjD in November 2024 
  • U.S. FDA granted Priority Review in gMG in Q4 2024 and wAIHA in Q2 2026

  • Late-breaking data from Phase 3 investigational study presented at the American College of Rheumatology Convergence show 58% of ICOTYDE-treated patients achieved an ACR20 response and 29% achieved an ACR50 response at Week 16
  • ICOTYDE is a first-in-class IL-23R targeted oral peptide, demonstrating significant joint and skin improvements and a favorable safety profile in a once-daily pill

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., Nov. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced positive results from a Phase 3 study investigating ICOTYDE® (icotrokinra) in biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA).a,b ICOTYDE is the first and only targeted oral peptide that precisely blocks the IL-23 receptor.1 ICOTYDE met the primary endpoint, with 58% of patients achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20) response compared with 41% receiving placebo at Week 16.2 Safety findings were consistent with the established safety profile of ICOTYDE, with no new safety signals identified. These results are being presented as a late-breaking poster at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026.

Psoriatic arthritis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory disease that can affect both the joints and skin.3,4 Nearly 30 percent of people with plaque psoriasis also develop psoriatic arthritis.5,6 It can cause pain, stiffness and swelling in and around the joints, along with the skin lesions associated with plaque psoriasis.7 Because inflammation can lead to progressive disease, there remains a need for treatment approaches that address the multiple ways psoriatic arthritis can affect patients. In clinical studies, ACR response is a composite measure whereby ACR20 represents ≥20% improvement in tender joint count, swollen joint count and other measures of disease activity. ACR50 and ACR70 use the same framework but represent ≥50% and ≥70% improvement, respectively.

"The significant joint responses observed in this study show the exciting potential for ICOTYDE, a targeted oral peptide therapy, to open an entirely new chapter in treating psoriatic arthritis with an oral option," said Joseph F. Merola, MD MMSc, Rheumatologist, Dermatologist, President of the Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis Multicenter Advancement Network, Co-President of the Group for Research in Psoriasis and Psoriatic Arthritis and President of the Rheumatologic Dermatology Society.d "Effective management of psoriatic arthritis requires addressing both joint and skin disease, and patients continue to need treatment options that can provide meaningful improvement across both."

ICOTYDE demonstrated joint and skin improvements through Week 242

The Phase 3 ICONIC-PsA 1 study met its primary endpoint, with a significantly higher proportion of patients receiving ICOTYDE 200 mg achieving an American College of Rheumatology 20 (ACR20)c response compared with placebo (58% vs. 41%) at Week 16. Numerically higher proportions of patients receiving ICOTYDE also achieved ACR50 (29% vs. 16%) and ACR70 (13% vs. 5%). Among patients with qualifying skin involvement, 57% receiving ICOTYDE achieved clear or almost clear skin (Investigator's Global Assessment [IGA] 0/1)e, compared with 14% receiving placebo (nominal p<0.001), while 37% achieved a Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI)f score of 90 compared with 6% receiving placebo (nominal p<0.001).

Response rates with ICOTYDE 200 mg continued to increase numerically through Week 24, with 69% of patients achieving ACR20, 40% achieving ACR50, and 18% achieving ACR70. Among patients with qualifying baseline skin involvement (BSA)g, 64% achieved clear or almost clear skin (IGA 0/1) and 56% achieved PASI 90. Safety data through Week 24 were consistent with the established safety profile of ICOTYDE, with no new safety signals identified.

"Many people living with psoriatic arthritis are still searching for treatments that can effectively address the full burden of their disease," said David M. Lee, M.D., Ph.D., Global Immunology Therapeutic Area Head, Johnson & Johnson. "These new findings underscore the potential of ICOTYDE to meaningfully improve outcomes in psoriatic arthritis and add to the growing body of evidence across psoriatic disease."

Editor's notes:

a. ICONIC-PsA 1 is an investigational Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating the efficacy and safety of once-daily oral icotrokinra in biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis. At Week 16, participants in the placebo group who were still on study treatment crossed over to receive ICOTYDE.
b. ICOTYDE is not approved for the treatment of active PsA.
c. American College of Rheumatology 20/50/70 (ACR20/50/70) response is defined as at least a 20%/50%/70% improvement in both tender and swollen joint counts and at least a 20%/50%/70% improvement in three of five other measures of disease activity.8
d. Dr. Joseph Merola is a paid consultant for Johnson & Johnson. He has not been compensated for any media work.
e. The Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) is a five-point scale with a severity score ranging from 0 to 4, where 0 indicates clear, 1 is minimal, 2 is mild, 3 is moderate, and 4 indicates severe disease.9
f. The Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) score grades the amount of surface area on each body region that is covered by psoriasis plaques and the severity of plaques for their redness, thickness and scaliness. PASI 100 corresponds to an improvement of 100% in PASI score from baseline.10
g. Patients with a baseline plaque psoriasis body surface area (BSA) ≥3% and IGA score ≥2.

About the ICONIC clinical development program

Phase 3 studies investigating ICOTYDE in active psoriatic arthritis include:

  • ICONIC-PsA 1 (NCT06878404) is a RCT to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ICOTYDE compared to placebo for the treatment of biologic-naïve participants with active PsA.11
  • ICONIC-PsA 2 (NCT06807424) is a RCT to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ICOTYDE compared to placebo for the treatment of biologic-experienced and biologic-naïve participants with active PsA.12

Pivotal Phase 3 studies in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis include:

  • ICONIC-LEAD (NCT06095115) is a RCT to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ICOTYDE compared with placebo in participants with moderate-to-severe plaque PsO.13
  • ICONIC-TOTAL (NCT06095102) is a RCT to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ICOTYDE compared with placebo for the treatment of PsO in participants with at least moderate severity affecting special areas (e.g., scalp, genital, and/or hands and feet).14
  • ICONIC-ADVANCE 1 (NCT06143878) and ICONIC-ADVANCE 2 (NCT06220604) are RCTs to evaluate the efficacy and safety of ICOTYDE compared with both placebo and deucravacitinib in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque PsO.15,16

Additional studies underway include: ICONIC-UC (NCT071196748) in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis; and ICONIC-CD (NCT7196722) in moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.17,18,19

About psoriatic arthritis

Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a chronic, immune-mediated, inflammatory disease characterized by peripheral joint inflammation, enthesitis (pain where the bone, tendon and ligament meet), dactylitis (a type of inflammation in the fingers and toes that can result in a swollen, sausage-like appearance), axial disease and the skin lesions associated with plaque psoriasis (PsO).20,3,4 The disease causes pain, stiffness and swelling in and around the joints; it commonly appears between the ages of 30 and 50, but can develop at any age.21 Nearly half of patients with PsA experience moderate fatigue and about one-third suffer from severe fatigue as measured by the modified fatigue severity scale.22 In patients with PsA, comorbidities such as obesity, cardiovascular disease, anxiety and depression are often present.23 Studies show up to 30% of people with plaque PsO also develop PsA.5,6 

About ICOTYDE® (icotrokinra) 

ICOTYDE® (icotrokinra) is the only targeted oral peptide designed to precisely block the IL-23 receptor, which underpins the inflammatory response in moderate-to-severe plaque PsO.1,24,25 ICOTYDE binds to the IL-23 receptor with single-digit picomolar affinity and demonstrated potent, precise inhibition of IL-23 signaling in human T cells.26 Clinical significance of these findings is unknown.

ICOTYDE is currently approved in the U.S. for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque PsO in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who weigh at least 40 kg who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Patients on ICOTYDE take one pill, once daily upon waking with water on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before eating.27

ICOTYDE was jointly discovered and is being developed pursuant to the license and collaboration agreement between Protagonist and Johnson & Johnson. Johnson & Johnson retains exclusive worldwide rights to develop ICOTYDE in Phase 2 clinical trials and beyond, and to commercialize compounds derived from the research conducted pursuant to the agreement against a broad range of indications.28,29,30

ICOTYDE is also being studied in active psoriatic arthritis, moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis and moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.12,13,14

ICOTYDE INDICATION AND IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

WHAT IS ICOTYDE (icotrokinra)?

ICOTYDE 200 mg is a prescription medicine used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and children 12 years of age and older who weigh at least 88 pounds (40 kg), who may benefit from taking injections or medicines by mouth (systemic therapy) or treatment using ultraviolet or UV light (phototherapy).

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about ICOTYDE?

  • Infections. Medicines that interact with the immune system, such as ICOTYDE, may lower your ability to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Your healthcare provider may check you for infections and tuberculosis (TB) before starting treatment and may treat you for TB before you begin treatment with ICOTYDE if you have a history of TB or have active TB. Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during and after treatment with ICOTYDE.

Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have any infection or have symptoms of an infection, including:

  • fever, sweat, or chills
  • cough
  • shortness of breath
  • blood in your mucus (phlegm)
  • muscle aches

 

  • warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body different from your psoriasis
  • weight loss
  • diarrhea or stomach pain
  • burning when you urinate or urinating more often than normal

Before taking ICOTYDE, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have an infection that does not go away or that keeps coming back.
  • have tuberculosis (TB) or have been in close contact with someone with TB.
  • have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). Avoid receiving live vaccines during treatment with ICOTYDE.
  • have kidney problems. 
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if ICOTYDE can harm your unborn baby.

Pregnancy Safety Study. There is a pregnancy safety study for women who take ICOTYDE during pregnancy. The purpose of this study is to collect information about the health of you and your baby. If you are pregnant or become pregnant during treatment with ICOTYDE, you can report your pregnancy by calling 1-800-526-7736 or visiting www.ICOTYDE.com.

  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if ICOTYDE passes into your breast milk. Talk to your healthcare provider about the best way to feed your baby during treatment with ICOTYDE.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

What are the possible side effects of ICOTYDE?

ICOTYDE may cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about ICOTYDE?"

The most common side effects of ICOTYDE include:

  • headache
  • nausea
  • cough

  • fungal infection
  • tiredness

These are not all the possible side effects of ICOTYDE. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch, or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

How should I take ICOTYDE?

  • Take ICOTYDE exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to take it.
  • Take ICOTYDE 1 time a day when you wake up on an empty stomach with water. Wait at least 30 minutes after taking ICOTYDE before eating food.
  • If you have difficulty swallowing tablets, ICOTYDE can be dispersed in water. For more information, please read the Medication Guide.
  • If you miss a dose of ICOTYDE, take the dose as soon as you remember and go back to your regular schedule the next day.

Please read the full Prescribing Information, including Medication Guide, for ICOTYDE and discuss any questions that you have with your doctor.

  • ALKIVIA met its primary and key secondary endpoints in the combined IMNM and DM population
  • First Phase 3 study to demonstrate statistically significant and clinically meaningful benefit in IMNM, an autoimmune myositis subtype with no approved therapies
  • Consistent, clinically meaningful treatment effect in DM, demonstrating improvements in muscle strength and skin disease activity

November 7, 2026, 10:00 AM ET

Amsterdam, the Netherlands – argenx SE (Euronext & Nasdaq: ARGX), the immunology innovation company, today announced that data from the Phase 3 ALKIVIA study demonstrating rapid and sustained improvement with VYVGART® Hytrulo (efgartigimod alfa and hyaluronidase-qvfc) in patients with autoimmune myositis will be featured in a late-breaking oral presentation (#LB24) at the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Convergence 2026 on November 11, 2026, from 9:15-9:30 a.m. ET.

Combined IMNM and DM population: Primary and key secondary endpoints met
The study met its primary endpoint in the combined immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) and dermatomyositis (DM) patient population, demonstrating that patients treated with efgartigimod achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 15.4-point greater improvement in mean Total Improvement Score (TIS) at Week 52 versus placebo (p=0.0011; 48.0 vs 32.6). The study also met key secondary endpoints in the combined population, including response rate, time to response, muscle strength, and disease activity.

Efgartigimod was generally well tolerated by patients. The observed safety profile was consistent with prior studies and the known safety profile of efgartigimod.

“These Phase 3 results add to the growing body of evidence that targeting FcRn delivers a meaningful, sustained benefit for people with autoimmune myositis,” said Luc Truyen, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer, argenx. “ALKIVIA demonstrates the clinical relevance of reducing pathogenic autoantibodies, strengthening the case for efgartigimod to be the first targeted treatment for IMNM. We are moving with urgency to bring efgartigimod to people living with IMNM, who have no approved treatments, and we remain committed to advancing efgartigimod for people living with DM.”

IMNM: Rapid, sustained improvement supports potential first approved treatment
IMNM patients treated with efgartigimod demonstrated a clinically meaningful 14.8-point greater improvement in mean TIS versus placebo at Week 52 (p=0.0048; 45.1 vs 30.2).

  • Early, durable response: A greater proportion of patients treated with efgartigimod achieved a mean TIS of 40 or more (TIS ≥ 40) at Week 52 versus those on placebo (22.0 percentage-point difference) and were twice as likely to maintain that response through Week 52.
  • Greater muscle strength: Patients treated with efgartigimod experienced greater improvement (5.4 points) versus placebo in Manual Muscle Testing-8 (MMT-8), which evaluates strength across eight muscle groups.
  • Reduced muscle injury: Creatine kinase (CK) levels decreased rapidly in patients treated with efgartigimod and remained lower through Week 52, with a 43.5 percentage-point greater reduction from baseline versus placebo, as well as greater improvement in CK grade (0.9-grade greater reduction). CK is a key biomarker of active muscle injury.
  • Improvements in disease activity: Patients and physicians both reported greater improvement in disease activity with efgartigimod versus placebo at Week 52 as measured by the Patient Global Assessment of Disease Activity (PGA) and Physician Global Assessment of Disease Activity (MDGA).

Based on the ALKIVIA results, argenx plans to submit a Supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for efgartigimod in IMNM by the end of 2026, supported by a Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the FDA.

DM: Clinically meaningful treatment effect supports targeting FcRn
In the DM patient population, a clinically meaningful 14.5-point greater improvement versus placebo in mean TIS at Week 52 was observed (p=0.1093; 51.5 vs 37.0), though statistical significance was not reached in this smaller cohort.

  • Early, sustained response: A greater proportion of patients treated with efgartigimod achieved TIS ≥ 40 versus placebo (27.2 percentage-point difference). Separation from placebo patients was evident from Week 4 and maintained through Week 52.
  • Improved skin disease: Patients treated with efgartigimod showed a clear improvement in skin disease severity (5.6-point greater improvement at Week 52) versus placebo, as measured by the Cutaneous Dermatomyositis Disease Area and Severity Index (CDASI), with improvement seen from Week 4.
  • Improved disease activity: Patients and physicians both reported greater improvement in disease activity with efgartigimod versus placebo at Week 52, as measured by the PGA and MDGA.

More information on the data presented at the ACR Convergence 2026 Annual Meeting can be found here. 

About the ALKIVIA Study
The ALKIVIA study was a global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, operationally seamless Phase 2/3 study of efgartigimod SC for the treatment of autoimmune myositis across immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM), dermatomyositis (DM) and polymyositis (PM). The ALKIVIA study randomized 265 patients who had active disease and were on background treatment. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive weekly injections of efgartigimod PH20 SC or matched placebo PH20 SC. The study was conducted in two phases, with an analysis of the Phase 2 portion of the clinical trial after the first 89 patients completed the study, followed by Phase 3. In the Phase 3 study, 175 patients received treatment. The Phase 3 study included a protocol-mandated corticosteroid taper throughout the study. The primary endpoint of Phase 3 was the mean Total Improvement Score (TIS) at the end of the treatment period of 52 weeks of all treated patients compared to placebo. Prespecified analyses evaluated the combined IMNM and DM population and each subtype separately. 

ALKIVIA was conducted globally across North and South America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, including China and Japan. argenx has an exclusive license agreement with Zai Lab for the development and commercialization of VYVGART and VYVGART Hytrulo in Greater China. Through this agreement, Zai Lab recruited Chinese patients into the ALKIVIA trial.  

About Autoimmune Myositis  
Autoimmune myositis is a heterogenous disease spectrum with autoimmune-mediated pathophysiology, characterized by chronic inflammation and progressive muscle weakness, and in some subtypes by skin involvement and other extramuscular manifestations. Proximal muscle weakness is a hallmark clinical feature across subtypes.  

Approximately 100,000 people in the United States live with autoimmune myositis, including approximately 20,000 with immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) and approximately 40,000 with dermatomyositis (DM). Up to 80% of patients report long-term disability despite treatment. There are currently no selectively targeted treatments available, and care and treatment relies primarily on corticosteroids and broad immunosuppressants, which are associated with significant cumulative toxicity, including metabolic, cardiovascular, musculoskeletal and infectious complications.  

Advances in the understanding of autoimmune myositis biology have highlighted the central role of antibody-mediated immunity, with pathogenic IgG autoantibodies contributing to muscle fiber damage and extramuscular manifestations across subtypes. FcRn maintains circulating IgG levels by recycling IgG antibodies, including pathogenic autoantibodies.  

About Immune-mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a subtype of autoimmune myositis and is characterized as a sudden and severe loss of muscle strength, progressing to difficulty walking, lifting arms, or maintaining independent mobility. The rapid onset and aggressive nature of the disease can often lead to hospitalization, intensive treatment, and reliance on caregivers, which can make the patient experience acute and destabilizing. As the disease progresses, healthy muscle tissue is permanently replaced by fat and scar tissue. Approximately 20,000 IMNM patients are diagnosed in the U.S.

About Dermatomyositis
Dermatomyositis (DM) is a subtype of autoimmune myositis and is characterized as muscle weakness and distinctive skin rashes that can be painful, itchy, or highly visible on the face, chest, and hands. DM can also be associated with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and is strongly associated with malignancy. Some patients have reported increased self-consciousness, stigma, and social withdrawal, making the emotional burden more pronounced. Approximately 40,000 DM patients are diagnosed in the U.S.

About Efgartigimod and Efgartigimod SC
Efgartigimod (efgartigimod alfa fcab) is a human IgG1 antibody fragment that binds to the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), resulting in the reduction of circulating IgG autoantibodies. It is the first approved FcRn blocker for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) globally, and for primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in Japan. Efgartigimod SC is a subcutaneous combination of efgartigimod alfa and recombinant human hyaluronidase PH20 (rHuPH20), Halozyme’s ENHANZE® drug delivery technology to facilitate subcutaneous injection delivery of biologics.

What is VYVGART HYTRULO® (efgartigimod alfa and hyaluronidase-qvfc)?
VYVGART HYTRULO is a prescription medicine used to treat adults with:

  • generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG)
  • chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP)

It is not known if VYVGART HYTRULO is safe and effective in children.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION
Do not take VYVGART HYTRULO if you are allergic to efgartigimod alfa, hyaluronidase, or any of the ingredients in VYVGART HYTRULO. VYVGART HYTRULO can cause serious allergic reactions and a decrease in blood pressure leading to fainting.

Before taking VYVGART HYTRULO, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have an infection or fever.
  • have recently received or are scheduled to receive any vaccinations.
  • have any history of allergic reactions.
  • have kidney (renal) problems.
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known whether VYVGART HYTRULO will harm your unborn baby.
    • Pregnancy Exposure Registry. There is a pregnancy exposure registry for women who use VYVGART HYTRULO during pregnancy. The purpose of this registry is to collect information about your health and your baby. Your healthcare provider can enroll you in this registry. You may also enroll yourself or get more information about the registry by calling 1-855-272-6524 or going to VYVGARTPregnancy.com
  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if VYVGART HYTRULO passes into your breast milk.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

VYVGART HYTRULO can cause side effects which can be serious, including:

  • Infection. VYVGART HYTRULO may increase the risk of infection. If you have an active infection, your healthcare provider should delay your treatment with VYVGART HYTRULO until your infection is gone. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you get any of the following signs and symptoms of an infection:

  • fever
  • pain and blockage of nasal passages
  • sore throat
  • chills
  • wheezing
  • excess phlegm
  • frequent and painful urination
  • shortness of breath
  • nasal discharge
  • cough
  
  • Allergic reactions (hypersensitivity reactions). VYVGART HYTRULO can cause allergic reactions that can be severe. These reactions can happen during, shortly after, or weeks after your VYVGART HYTRULO injection. Tell your healthcare provider or get emergency help right away if you have any of the following symptoms of an allergic reaction:

  • rash
  • trouble breathing
  • swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue
  • low blood pressure
  • shortness of breath
  • fainting
  • hives
 
  • Infusion or injection-related reactions. VYVGART HYTRULO can cause infusion or injection-related reactions. These reactions can happen during or shortly after your VYVGART HYTRULO injection. Tell your healthcare provider if you have any of the following symptoms of an infusion or injection-related reaction:

  • high blood pressure
  • shivering
  • chills
  • chest, stomach, or back pain

The most common side effects of VYVGART HYTRULO include respiratory tract infection, headache, urinary tract infection, and injection site reactions.

These are not all the possible side effects of VYVGART HYTRULO. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Key Terms

restricted stock unitsfinancial
Restricted stock units are a type of company reward where employees are promised shares of stock, but they only fully own these shares after meeting certain conditions, like staying with the company for a set time. Investors care because these awards affect future share count, executive incentives, and signal how management’s success will be measured and rewarded.
adjusted ebitdafinancial
Adjusted EBITDA is a way companies measure how much money they make from their core operations, like running a business, by removing certain costs or income that aren’t part of regular business activities. It helps investors see how well a company is doing without distractions from unusual expenses or gains, making it easier to compare companies or track performance over time.
nasdaq listing rule 5635(c)(4)regulatory

This helps protect investors by making sure the company doesn't flood the market with new shares without their say, which could lower the stock's value.

Calgary, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - Prospera Energy Inc. (TSXV: PEI) (OTC Pink: GXRFF) ("Prospera", "PEI", the "Corporation", or the "Company") reaffirms its commitment to clean up every outstanding environmental obligation site and resolve every compliance issue across its Saskatchewan fields, working closely with the Saskatchewan Ministry of Energy and Resources (the "Ministry"), landowners, rural municipalities and local vendors. The Company has confirmed the support of its senior secured lender and key stakeholders on this commitment and all its active wells remain online and producing at this time.

Prospera's Commitment: Every Site at the Monitoring Stage by January 22, 2027

Prospera is committed to cleaning up the 13 environmental sites named in Minister's Order MRO 98/26, most of which predate current management, and to restoring each to its original condition. To date since Oct 31, 2024, the Company has invested $2.83 million in spill response, site assessment and remediation, logged 1,646 field hours with local crews, hauled 6,662 tonnes of contaminated soil to an approved landfill and isolated or repaired four failed pipelines. 11 of the 13 sites are at or past Phase II assessment. Prospera has given the Ministry the following site-by-site schedule:

  • November 15, 2026: legacy spill piles at Cuthbert 08-28, 02-28 and 01-28 removed, with confirmatory testing to begin.
  • November 27, 2026: Hearts Hill 04-20, 16-28 and 05-20 and Luseland 12-28 at the monitoring stage, with remediation as laboratory results are received.
  • December 15, 2026: Hearts Hill 09-20 and both 09-19 sites at the monitoring stage; results for the 09-19 sites have been submitted to the Ministry's Kindersley office and are awaiting their approval to backfill.
  • December 25, 2026: Phase II assessments complete at Cuthbert 02-02 and 12-27.
  • December 31, 2026: Hearts Hill 08-28, the site of a September 2026 pipeline release, at the monitoring stage.
  • January 22, 2027: all five Cuthbert sites at the monitoring stage.

Topsoil replacement and seeding on reclaimed areas will follow in spring 2027.

Resolving Compliance Items

The Ministry's inspection records show open items reduced from 146 in October 2024 to 58 today, with 352 of 410 items closed.

  • All 2026 annulus testing is complete; failed wells are shut in and packer repairs have been completed.
  • The Vegetation Management Plan is complete, with all three areas cut and sprayed multiple times this season.
  • Inspection corrections and fixes have been uploaded consistently to the Ministry's IRIS system for re-inspection.
  • The Abandonment, Reclamation, and Reactivation Plan is complete, and a 30-well program has been costed.
  • Every well on an expired freehold lease has been reviewed and is being renewed or abandoned.

Working with the Ministry

Prospera is working hand in hand with the Ministry to see this through. It has met with the Ministry and filed a written progress report every two weeks for the past 2 years, has offered weekly reporting until every site is at monitoring stage or closed, has invited Ministry staff to visit the sites, and follows the Ministry's written guidance on what each site must show to reach the monitoring stage. A dedicated compliance team reports directly to the CEO and reviews every obligation weekly.

Minister's Order MRO 196/26 suspends Prospera's Saskatchewan licences in stages beginning November 29, 2026. Prospera has asked the Province for a written, performance-based path to rescind the Order, based on the milestones the Company meets over the next 7 to 21 days and the significant environmental field work that was already underway throughout September, October, and early November.

Working with the Community

Prospera is a long-term partner to the communities around its fields:

  • Landowners: Prospera has paid $6.6 million in surface lease payments to area farmers and landowners since 2021, and an active reclamation program is cleaning up leases left by prior operators.
  • Local vendors: Since new management took over in October 2024, Prospera has reduced the legacy and active vendors it inherited who still have outstanding balances from 660 to 306, settling one creditor at a time through active communication. Its field work is carried out by local trucking, service-rig, chemical and field-service companies whose outstanding balances have been brought down considerably both in dollar amounts and aging schedule.
  • Reactivating existing wells: Through reactivations of inactive wells, Prospera has taken Luseland production from 54 to 284 bbl/d. Its first ten restarted wells cost $1.14 million and have generated $2.19 million in profit, and nine of the ten have paid out in about 11 months on average, bringing work and commerce back to the towns around Luseland, Macklin and Kindersley.
  • Beyond the field: Prospera sponsors Stigma-Free Mental Health's ILLUMINATE event on oil-sector and rural mental health; charity events for Brown Bagging for Calgary's Kids, pediatric cancer care and youth sport; the Straz Strong Foundation of Humboldt Broncos survivors; and University of Alberta Petroleum Engineering student events.

"We are committed to restoring every one of these sites and resolving every outstanding compliance item at an accelerated pace, and our crews have been and are on site today," said Shubham Garg, Chairman and CEO of Prospera. "We have given the Province a firm schedule, with every site at the monitoring stage by January 22, and we will meet it. Saskatchewan's landowners, municipalities and local businesses are our partners in this, and we intend to have our fields clean, compliant and a source of good work for the communities around them, including obligations we inherited when our new management team came into Prospera in October 2024."

Cancellation of Equity Financing

As a result of Minister's Order MRO 196/26 (the "Order"), Prospera has cancelled its previously announced $12 million equity financing which had been scheduled to close on November 7, 2026.

Commitment to Updates

Prospera will issue a further update on its environmental remediation program and progress at every key milestone, and issue a further update on its discussions with the Ministry regarding the Order as material developments occur. The update will report progress against each milestone in the schedule above, including the removal of the Cuthbert spill piles by November 15 and the sites reaching monitoring stage by November 27. Prospera will continue to report regularly to the Ministry and will keep shareholders, landowners and the communities where it operates informed as the work proceeds.

About Prospera

Prospera Energy Inc. is a publicly traded Canadian energy company specializing in the exploration, development, and production of crude oil and natural gas. Headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, Prospera is dedicated to optimizing recovery from legacy fields using environmentally safe and efficient reservoir development methods and production practices. The company's core properties are strategically located in Saskatchewan and Alberta, including Cuthbert, Luseland, Hearts Hill, and Brooks. Prospera Energy Inc. is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol PEI and the U.S. OTC Market under GXRFF.

Prospera reports gross production at the first point of sale, excluding gas used in operations and volumes from partners in arrears, even if cash proceeds are received. Gross production represents Prospera's working interest before royalties, while net production reflects its working interest after royalty deductions. These definitions align with CSA Staff Notice 51-324 to ensure consistency and transparency in reporting.
